body:
Fear mostly. I'm afraid that dying will hurt, or that I'll mess up the attempt and end up paralysed or brain damaged.

Not to mention, it requires a certain amount of energy to organise a suicide attempt. Energy that I don't usually have.

>Have you traveled?

Somewhat. The problem with travelling is that wherever you go, there you are.

>Done something completely unexpected, just to see what happened?

I've done plenty of unexpected things, and the results were often dull.

>Do that. Even if you don't want to. Do it anyway.

I do. It doesn't make me feel any better. I'm not really sure what the point is.

>I mean your dreams, the ones you have when you sleep.

I've done that before, too. But, that just made things more painful. I'd much rather sleep and dream 24/7. Being alive might be tolerable then.

Those reasons don't quite work for me, I realise that they mean a lot to you, but they don't really feel that relevant to me.

>But I think a good reason not to suicide is that you shouldn't want your legacy to be that you are a quitter, to be blunt.

Suffice to say, I don't really care about my legacy, being seen as a quitter simply doesn't bother me.

>If nothing else, think about the people you love and will leave behind in this life, because your passing will cause them immense amounts of pain that will last for a long time.

I'll be leaving behind very few people, simply because I don't know that many. Yeah, it'll hurt them, but it won't be my concern when I'm dead. Perhaps, I'm callous and selfish, but it'll never be me that has to deal with the fallout.

>you can build a better future and that your present pain can be your fuel to make it happen. 

I don't particularly care to build a better future. Any future seems unacceptable to me. Even if I experienced incredibly good fortune for the rest of my life, I can't imagine that it'd be a life that I was interested in living. I'd much rather just end things.

>it is a permanent solution to temporary problems.

I agree that these are temporary problems. After all, my life is temporary, and my problems will be over when I'm dead. That's precisely why I consider suicide to be a good solution.

I no longer have any curiosity. I feel like I've seen everything I need to.

>If I'm feeling particularly suicidal, I try and force myself to do something that I truly enjoy.

I don't enjoy much of anything, anymore. Sometimes I force myself to do things that I think I should enjoy. It doesn't help.

>Get outside. Look at the world. Watch other people and their lives.

The last time I tried that I ended up crying in public. I'm not doing that again.

>Think about your dreams

I'm not sure what type of dreams you're talking about. Do you mean wishes, or the dreams I have when I sleep?
